descriptionChirho: A loud disturbance, disorderly noise, or public commotion, often involving a crowd or mob. All three clusters are case variants (nominative, genitive, accusative) of the same noun with identical meaning. Translations are completely uniform across languages: 'uproar/tumult/commotion' (eng), 'alboroto/tumulto' (spa), 'ghasia' (swa: disturbance, used in all three clusters), 'hangaama/halchal/shor-gul' (hin: uproar/agitation/noise), 'shaghab/idtiraab' (arb: riot/disturbance), 'sodong/sollan' (kor: disturbance/disorder). No semantic distinction exists between these inflectional forms.
